title: Long delay echoes behind Sagan's Contact
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Long delay echoes behind Sagan's Contact, about 1920s-1930s at Earth radio, and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: I think he's talking about these long delay echoes which are this phenomena that occurred in the 1920s and 30s at the invention of the radio

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, says that the astronomer Carl Sagan's novel Contact, about humans receiving a message from aliens, may be drawing on long delay echoes. These, Michels says, were strange radio signals heard coming back seconds after they were sent, reported in the 1920s and 30s when radio was new. If true, some have taken them as a hint that something out in space was answering.
